property_summary: For any caller and any timestamp, calling fallback with exactly 10 ether always updates pastBlockTime (i.e., the call succeeds and pastBlockTime becomes > previous value), whereas the mutant requiring 9 ether will fail to accept calls that send 10 ether and thus can leave pastBlockTime unchanged for such inputs — so the reference always accepts value==10 ether calls and updates pastBlockTime, but the mutant does not for those inputs.

For any caller and any timestamp/block, calling fallback with msg.value == 10 ether succeeds and advances pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 (the reference always accepts 10 ether payments and updates pastBlockTime; the mutant that requires 9 ether will reject 10 ether and thus can leave pastBlockTime unchanged for inputs where msg.value == 10 ether).

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether to fallback, the reference contract never updates pastBlockTime when the current block.timestamp is <= previous pastBlockTime (such calls revert), whereas the mutant allows such calls to succeed and update pastBlockTime — so the property is that a call with timestamp <= stored pastBlockTime always reverts in the reference but may succeed in the mutant.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether to C's fallback, if the current block.timestamp is less-than-or-equal-to C.pastBlockTime then the call must revert (so pastBlockTime must remain unchanged); the mutant that removes the timestamp check can accept such calls and update pastBlockTime, violating this rule.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether to C.fallback, if the call is made at a timestamp <= C.pastBlockTime then the reference contract always reverts (leaving pastBlockTime unchanged), whereas the mutant (which removed the timestamp check) can accept such a call and update pastBlockTime — so the property is that calls at timestamp <= pastBlockTime must not succeed.

After any successful fallback call that required msg.value == 10 ether and passed the timestamp check, the contract's public pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the moment of the call completion; the mutant that stores block.timestamp (not +1) can produce pastBlockTime == block.timestamp and thus violates this for some inputs.

After any successful fallback call (which requires msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime), the reference contract sets pastBlockTime to strictly greater than the block.timestamp at completion (block.timestamp + 1), while the mutant sets it to block.timestamp and can therefore make pastBlockTime == block.timestamp for some inputs.

For any caller and valid call (msg.value == 10 ether and timestamp > pastBlockTime), the reference contract only forwards the entire balance back to the caller when block.number % 15 == 0; therefore after any admissible fallback call the contract's balance is zero if and only if block.number % 15 == 0 — the mutant always empties the contract, violating this conditional behavior for some blocks.
